Negative energy (%s kWh) at stage "%s" on %s. Two common causes: the meter has just been replaced without being marked, or two readings have had their dates swapped.
The row could not be fetched because the chain has no stage marked as "PR numerator". It deliberately does not fall back to the sales stage — the two reference points differ by a few per cent.

A stage with neither a meter nor a tag has to be filled in by someone every day. That is acceptable — auxiliary consumption often has no meter of its own — but it should be plain which stages are like that.
The running total is recomputed on every read, not stored. Correct a day mid-month and every day after it is right at once, with nothing to re-run.

Declare the stages the electricity passes through, from the generating\n               equipment to the sales meter. Declared once and used for every day —\n               and the same structure works for both wind and solar.

The stage used as the AC energy when computing the performance ratio.\n\nDIFFERENT from the sales stage, and it has to be declared separately. Checked against a real report from an operating plant: their PR numerator is 3% lower than the energy at the sales meter — because PR is measured over its own operating window, shorter than the whole day. Treating the two as one is being 3% wrong while still looking plausible.

Only ENERGY stages take part in the loss-by-stage calculation.

Auxiliary and overnight consumption are intentional use — fold them into losses and the figure swells with nobody able to trace why.

A standalone measurement point is measured for another purpose and does not lie on the path of the electricity — for example the energy used as the PR numerator, which is measured over its own window. Leave it in the chain and it enters the subtraction and produces a meaningless loss figure.

Order the stages along the path the electricity takes, from the generating equipment out to the grid. The loss is computed between each stage and the one immediately before it — so the order is what decides the figure.
The auxiliary and overnight stages take no part in the subtraction: they are intentional consumption, not losses.
